transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-09
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~34 minutes
Attendees: Emily Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Nimbus - Head of ML), Tom Keller (Nimbus - Platform), Priya V. (Nimbus - Security), Luis Ortega (Nimbus - DevOps)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC check-in focused on onboarding blockers: creds, VPC peering, KMS/HSM clarity, and a fallback plan if dedicated capacity not ready. SE requested a focused benchmark and there was discussion about cost/latency tradeoffs and what tests matter to Nimbus.

Topics:
- Access provisioning and temporary credentials
- VPC peering and egress limitations in Nimbus environment
- KMS/HSM integration questions for private key storage
- Benchmark plan: KV cache efficacy, batching, and tail latency
- Fallback: hosted vs dedicated and conservative routing policies

Action items (recorded here, also in metadata): see action_items field

Transcript:
[00:00] Emily: All right, good afternoon everyone, uh thanks for joining. We'll do the quick 30 minute p o c check. Marcus and I will run through access items, then we'll triage blockers. Aisha, is now still good?
[00:08] Aisha: Yeah working good thanks. We have Tom and Priya on; Luis just joined.
[00:12] Marcus: Great, I'll start with the infra checklist. Tom, last week you mentioned you could get us a service account for staging — any updates?
[00:20] Tom: Yep, we spun up a staging project and I created the service account, but we're waiting on IAM role binding from security, Priya's team. There's a little policy around cross-project peering so that is the blocker.
[00:30] Priya: Sorry yeah, we need the least-privilege list from Redwood. We can't open peering until we confirm keys and KMS boundary. Also want to confirm whether Redwood needs HSM or just customer-managed KMS keys.
[00:42] Emily: Understandable. We'll share a minimal role doc today. As for KMS vs HSM, Marcus, do you want to outline options?
[00:48] Marcus: Sure. For the pilot we support three patterns: 1) Redwood-managed KMS (fastest), 2) customer-managed KMS with RBAC + key rotation, or 3) HSM-backed keys for FIPS/HSM needs. The actual runtime only needs the encryption-at-rest keys to unwrap model artifacts and to sign request logs if you want. HSM adds complexity and some latency for key ops but is supported.
[01:07] Aisha: If we go HSM that adds procurement timelines — we prefer customer-managed KMS for now. We need an audit trail though, so KMS logs + audit logs are important.
[01:18] Marcus: Yep, audit logs are kept. We can also send syslog/Cloudwatch exports. There might be a small delay in log propagation, but it's standard.
[01:26] Luis: Also, can Redwood support prefix/KV cache so our repeated clinical-combo prompts don't hammer cost? We're seeing lots of similar token prefixes.
[01:35] Marcus: Absolutely. We have prefix caching and KV cache support; in staging we'll enable caching and measure hit rate. The main tuning knobs are cache TTL, tokenization boundaries, and batch sizes. For throughput we typically recommend continuous batching with a 25-50ms aggregation window for low-latency apps.
[01:51] Tom: On batch sizes — what about peak latency? Our SLO is 120ms p50 and 400ms p95 for the patient triage path.
[02:00] Marcus: That's tight. On hosted API, with a smaller model quantized we can hit ~80-120ms p50 for 512 tokens on our low-latency tier. For p95 it depends on concurrent load and KV cache hit. For Dedicated GPUs the p95 is more stable but you trade higher cost. We'll run the 5k-token benchmark with your sample prompts to see numbers.
[02:19] Aisha: Good, what about fallback if Dedicated isn't ready? We need a plan to keep the app alive.
[02:24] Emily: Two options: 1) route to hosted model variants with capacity-aware routing (cost increases but keeps online), or 2) degrade model size/quantization in Dedicated. We can set automated fallback policies per route.
[02:38] Priya: Any data residency concerns? Some of our requests reference EHR snippets, even though they're pseudonymized. We need to ensure logs don't leak PII.
[02:47] Marcus: We recommend redaction at call-time and also can disable request body retention for that customer. For dedicated/private deployments, data stays in your VPC. For hosted, we can disable retention and provide access logs only.
[02:59] Tom: Ok we'll provide a sanitized prompt set for benchmarking.
[03:05] Marcus: Great, we'll run benchmarks on the sanitized set. Also want to call out cold-starts: if your workflow has bursty traffic, we'll see higher tail latency on cold KV caches. We recommend a warmup traffic pattern or scheduled warm containers.
[03:20] Aisha: Sounds reasonable. Quick question on costs — can Redwood provide an estimate for the pilot vs production? We need to show ops how cost scales.
[03:29] Emily: We'll provide a rough pro-forma after the benchmark. It will include tokens, compute hours for Dedicated, and egress estimates. We'll also show the effect of caching and lower quant profiles.
[03:40] Priya: On security reviews — I'd like a 30-60 minute session next week focused on SSO/SAML and KMS integration. Also will want to see SOC2 docs.
[03:50] Emily: We'll send SOC2 + ISO pack and propose a time. Marcus, can you lead the SSO deep-dive?
[03:56] Marcus: Yep, happy to. I'll prepare a diagram of SAML flows and where keys live.
[04:02] Luis: One more operational note — our networking team restricts egress so some external endpoints are blocked. Does Redwood require outgoing connections to third-party telemetry?
[04:11] Marcus: Not by default. You can opt into telemetry. For the pilot we'll keep telemetry off until you enable logs export. Runtime needs to reach Redwood endpoints only if you're using hosted control plane; for private deployment the control plane can be customer-hosted.
[04:26] Aisha: Any blockers you need from us now?
[04:30] Emily: Best blockers right now: 1) confirm service account + role bindings so SE can access staging; 2) provide sanitized prompt set for benchmark; 3) Priya to confirm KMS approach (customer-managed KMS preferred).
[04:41] Tom: We'll aim to have the IAM binding and sanitized prompts by Thursday.
[04:45] Priya: I'll review KMS requirements and get back by Monday.
[04:49] Marcus: We'll run two bench passes: a short latency-focused set and a long tail throughput pass. Expect results uploaded by Friday.
[04:56] Emily: Perfect. Recap of next steps and I'll send the security pack. Any final q's?
[05:02] Aisha: None from me, thanks.
[05:04] Tom: All good.
[05:05] Luis: good thanks.
[05:06] Emily: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
